metadata.name: Amino acid biosynthesis (overview)
metadata.description: Where the twenty amino acids come from: the central-carbon precursors (3-phosphoglycerate, PEP + erythrose-4P, pyruvate, oxaloacetate, 2-oxoglutarate, ribose-5P / PRPP) and the biosynthetic families built on them — serine, aromatic, pyruvate, aspartate, glutamate and histidine. Whole pathways are drawn as summary arrows (KEGG modules). After KEGG map01230; drawn by GEMs MAP.

scope.note: Families are universal; lysine is made from aspartate (DAP pathway, bacteria and plants) or from 2-oxoglutarate (AAA pathway, fungi). Animals lack several of these pathways (essential amino acids). Compartments are chosen by the person mapping onto a GEM.

metadata.license: MIT (drawing and curation); identifiers and biology from KEGG, MetaNetX and BiGG

citations.text: Kanehisa M, Goto S. KEGG: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes. Nucleic Acids Res 28:27-30 (2000)

source.generation_method: KEGG flat files + KGML (structure only) → curated biological graph → identities reconciled with MetaNetX (backend client) and the BiGG tables → hand-designed layout
